doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Learning orchestration from David Matthews and Emile Charlap
summary: New York arranger Matthews and contractor/copyist Charlap taught him to write for strings and French horns.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: write, things that I didn’t know how to write. And all that stuff, I said well how do you write for French horns, or how do you write for strings, the violin. And they would tell me, and I’ve got a whole year of education by just asking the question you know?
These were guys in the band?

No, they was New York — Emile Charlap was a New York contractor. He used to copy all my music for me, and he would show me what I did wrong and what I did right. You know I used to write all the parts out and I saw Dave Matthews, he was a fine arranger you know. And I would write things over and over again and he would draw lines, you know, from one part to another. You know and I said, “Can you do that?” And he said, “Yeah, you can do that.” And Emile would write it, he would transpose it for them you know, and when I learned that, that shortened my awake time you know. But that’s how I learned, by doing. I learned by doing.
I can picture that because I was listening to “Pass the Peas” you know, and you’ve got that line [scats]. You could just write it once and put 8 times.
